newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures rally on positive Tankan.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures rally on positive Tankan.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures rallied on Wednesday after better-than-expected results from the Bank of Japan's "Tankan" survey of corporate sentiment.
By the lunchtime close, the Nikkei 225 September contract was up 285 points at 20,660 after reaching an intra-day peak of 20,715. Volume was a healthy 8,755 lots.
"The market turned today on the better-than-expected Tankan," said one dealer. "It burst up through resistance at 20,300/400 and now looks comfortable."

The Tankan report showed confidence high among some of Japan's industrial sectors. Its key diffusion index for major manufacturers was plus seven, up from plus two in March and compared with economists' forecasts of minus four to plus four.
Many dealers had expected a bearish report.
Dealers said market sentiment was now buoyant but was still held in check by worries over inflationary pressures, which some dealers thought might eventually lead to higher interest rates.
One technical analyst said he now expected the market to consolidate, moving sideways to slightly higher in the next few days.
"It now has support at 20,300/400 points and resistance at around 20,750," he said. "If it closes over 20,750 tonight, 20,800/900 should be no problem. It all depends on today's closing," he added.
